Patch src/runloop/transaction.ts and src/runloop/types.ts (their current texts follow) and return both WHOLE. types.ts: CardOutcome gains the optional LAST member `lastRound?: "green" | "red"`; RunReport gains `stop?: string` between `requests?` and `fault?`; nothing else changes. transaction.ts: (1) drop the run-wide `batches` counter; keep per card its retries of this transaction; before a retry batch a blamed card is capped when its retries (W's included) are 2 (cap text "2 retries") or else its retries of this transaction are >= input.budget.maxRetryBatches (cap text "maxRetryBatches " + that number); any capped blamed card → stop = "retry cap: " + the capped blamed cards in deck order as "<customId> (<cap>)" joined ", ", then the rollback as now; (2) the retry batch runs by layers: import { layerGenerations } from "../cards/layer.js"; for each generation of layerGenerations(input.deck), in order, the blamed cards in it (skip an empty one) go to ONE processGeneration call, so a dependant's retry is compiled after its dependency's retry wrote; requests and usage in send order; (3) a rollback outcome's winningVariant is the state's variant (the attempt on the tree), and its last key is lastRound: "red" when its last round was red, "green" when green, the key absent when no round ran (W's rollback); (4) finish() sets report.stop (when set) before report.fault, so fault stays the last key. Every other behaviour (deadline, outside the subset, interrupt, thrown values, reasons, attempts, earlierFailures, written outcomes) stays exactly as it is. Write no test file: a probe tests you and a judge writes the example tests.

## Function Run Transaction

Write every card, then run every acceptance on the full tree, retry the owners of the red lines to a fixed point, commit all or nothing.

Behaviour: runTransaction(input, deps) → Promise<Run Result>; Run Deck calls it for a deck Transaction Deck marks, before anything else (src/runloop/deck.ts: `if (isTransactionDeck(input.deck.cards)) return runTransaction(input, deps);` as its first line; import from "./transaction.js" and "../cards/transaction.js"). owners: every target of every card → its customId (deck order, the first owner kept). before = Snapshot Targets(root, every target, deck order) — the run's starting tree. W = Write: runDeck(input with deck.cards each a copy with acceptance "true", externalDependsOn as given; deps with commit () => null) — Run Deck's generations, budget, interrupts, skips and retries of a card it could not write (corrupt, truncated, stale, compile), every written answer left on the tree. W.report.fault set, or some W outcome not "written" → rollback (below), no acceptance run. Else rounds r = 0, 1, …: every card in deck order runs ITS acceptance (Run Acceptance(card.acceptance, root, {env: deps.env, timeoutMs: deps.acceptanceTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS})); exit 0 green, else red with Blame Log(its log, its customId, owners, TREE_PROFILES' fileLine in order, p → a file or directory exists at root/p). All green → deps.commit(id, targets) per card in deck order, id = the customId of the attempt whose files are on the tree (the card's, or "<customId>.r<n>" of its last written retry); done. Some red: any outside line → fault "outside the subset: " + every red card's outside lines (each once, sorted) joined ", ", then rollback. Else blamed = every id some red card's Blame names, in deck order. A card's retries are its own (P24, issue #16 item 1; no run-wide count of retry batches, a round that blames other cards costs this card nothing): a blamed card is capped when its retries (W's included) are 2, cap "2 retries", or else when its retries of this transaction are >= input.budget.maxRetryBatches, cap "maxRetryBatches <m>" (m that number); some blamed card capped → the report's stop = "retry cap: " + every capped blamed card, deck order, as "<customId> (<cap>)", joined ", ", then rollback; deps.interrupted?.() a string s → throws Error "interrupted by <s>"; deps.now() >= input.budget.deadline → rollback, the blamed cards "budget-exceeded" reason "deadline" (no stop key: the reason names it). Else per blamed card, n its retries + 1: {...buildRetry(card, n, acceptanceOutput, previousDiff), acceptance: "true"}, acceptanceOutput = the logs of this round's red cards whose Blame names it, deck order, "\n"-joined; previousDiff = Build Attempt Diff(before's text of its targets (null when absent), the targets' text on disk now ("" when absent)); the retry batch runs by layers (P24, issue #16 item 2): the generations of Layer Generations(input.deck) in order, each restricted to the blamed cards, empty ones skipped, one processGeneration(that layer's retry cards, deps with commit () => null, root) per layer, so a dependant's retry is compiled after its dependency's retry wrote and is not stale; requests and usage in send order; a written retry's files are on the tree, a retry not written leaves them; then round r + 1. Outcomes: written → {customId, status "written", reason null, attempts: 1 + its retries (W's and these), winningVariant its last written attempt's, acceptanceLog its last round's log, earlierFailures: W's + its red round logs in order, commit and diffstat from the hook}. Rollback: before restored (Restore Snapshot); a card W did not write keeps W's outcome; every other → {status "failed" (or "budget-exceeded" above), reason: "outside the subset" when its last log named an outside line, else "acceptance failed" when its last round was red and its Blame names itself, else "transaction rolled back"; attempts 1 + its retries, winningVariant the variant whose files are on the tree at the rollback (W's, or its last written retry's; P24, issue #16 item 3), acceptanceLog its last round's log (W's when no round ran), earlierFailures W's + its red logs of rounds before the last, commit null, diffstat null, then lastRound "green" or "red" (its last round) when a round ran — absent when none ran}. CardOutcome gains the optional last key `lastRound?: "green" | "red"`, set only here; RunReport gains the optional key `stop?: string`, between requests and fault. A value thrown (an answer write, the interrupt, the hook): before the first commit → before restored and every card {status "skipped", reason "fault", attempts 0, winningVariant null, acceptanceLog "", earlierFailures [], commit null, diffstat null}; after → the committed keep "written", the rest that outcome, nothing restored; fault = the Error's message. The Run Report: runId, completedAt deps.now(), branch, processor deps.config.id, generations W's, outcomes in deck order, usageTotals W's plus every retry request's (cost null when none), requests W's rows then the retries' in send order, then stop and fault, each when set (fault the last key). deps.onVariant sees every request (W's verdicts are those of the "true" acceptance).

Steps:

- uses: language
- produces: Run Report

Data Run Report: The summary of one run (its schema and archive layout are runloop's; the file write and commit are P6 git's).
Schema:
{ runId: string, completedAt: number, branch: string, processor: string, generations: number, outcomes: CardOutcome[], usageTotals: { inputTokens: number, outputTokens: number, cost: number | null, requests: number }, requests?: RequestUsage[], fault?: string } — fault only when the run stopped on a fault; requests always set by Run Deck (optional for report literals built elsewhere)

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Write the files: `src/runloop/transaction.ts`, `src/runloop/types.ts`.

TypeScript with `strict` on, ESM with NodeNext resolution: every relative import carries the `.js` extension and types are imported with `import type`. No `any`: use `unknown` and narrow. Tests are vitest: `toBe` on scalars and short strings, `toStrictEqual` on a whole result; stubs come from `tests/helpers.ts`, never your own.
